hero.title: Bindusara: The Link of Empires
hero.description: Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, served as the vital bridge between the foundational era of Chandragupta and the expansionist epoch of Ashoka the Great.

items.decryption: Remember his title (Amitraghata), his dynasty, his relations with Greek monarchs, the Taxila revolts, and his successor Ashoka.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not confuse 'Amitraghata' (Slayer of foes) with 'Devanampiya' (Ashoka's title).
Do not assume he was a weak ruler; he maintained the vast empire inherited from Chandragupta without significant losses.
Remember, he was not the one who conquered Kalinga; that was Ashoka.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Consolidated empire from North to South (Karnataka).
  • Maintained stability in North-Western borderlands.

Personalities

  • Deimachus (Seleucid envoy).
  • Dionysius (Ptolemy II envoy).
  • Chanakya (Chief Advisor).
  • Political Legacy
    • Title: Amitraghata (Slayer of foes) - Greek source Amitrochates.
    • Diplomacy: Maintained friendly ties with Hellenistic world; requested figs, wine, and a philosopher from Antiochus I.
    • Internal Security: Suppressed revolts at Taxila due to oppressive governors; sent Ashoka to restore order.
  • Religious Inclination
    • Inclined towards the Ajivika sect.
    • Often associated with the influence of the seer Pingalavatsa.
